top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) is my first choice on the common criteria: a voice that is hard to confuse with any other, formal and linguistic ambition sustained at very large scale, and imaginative depth that builds memory, the body and dream into one project. As publicly described, Blinding (the first Orbitor volume) and Solenoid anchor the case. Attribution is clean, with one author and one principal language, and the prose-anchored citation claims no more than the committee has weighed. The unanimity of the openings is not merit evidence. The case survived the strongest alternatives, Adonis above all, mainly because the prose is more fully available to us than Arabic prosody. That reflects the limits of our evidence, not a smaller achievement. The reservations remain: whether Solenoid and the later novels deepen the project or only elaborate it, whether density stays purposeful, and how much Romanian rhythm survives translation. This judgment rests on public knowledge and translated reception, not on a full reading or independent verification. P000 is ranked last because the slate offers a credible single-writer proposal, and the open questions narrow the citation without defeating the case for an award.
